summary.headline: CleanMax Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose to INR45 crore from INR17 crore; FY26 EBITDA up 28% to INR1,295 crore with 1,400 MW added.
summary.overview: CleanMax reported Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA of about INR350 crore and PAT of INR45 crore versus INR17 crore a year earlier, with FY26 EBITDA up 28% to INR1,295 crore and FY26 PAT of about INR86 crore. Operational capacity reached about 3.1 GW, with 1,400 MW added in FY26 and 2.6 GW contracted but not yet executed. Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27 and flagged Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation about 30%) and the new DSM mechanism as open risks, without quantifying the DSM impact. No financial guidance was given, consistent with company policy.

segments.name: RE Power Sales
segments.commentary: Operational capacity about 3,100 MW plus 2,600 MW contracted but not executed, totalling 5.7 GW; gross margin about 92-93% and EBITDA margin about 83.5%, with about 90% of EBITDA from this segment.

segments.name: RE Services
segments.commentary: Operational capacity of 555 MW with another 215 MW under construction; EBITDA margin rose to about 19.6% from 14.4%, and revenue grew about 28-30%.

guidance_outlook: Minimum 1,500 MW of RE Power Sales capacity addition in FY27; management said it is very confident of achieving this.
No financial guidance given; management reiterated it does not forecast EBITDA, though reported EBITDA has historically been about 1.1x the prior run-rate EBITDA.
Around 1 GW of the FY27 additions is STU and the remaining CTU (including a 530 MW Koppal project, 450 MW wind and 80 MW solar, in Karnataka).
Long-term EBITDA margin on RE Power Sales expected to rise from about 83% to nearly 86% over 3-4 years.
Company to make an announcement in about three to four months on energy storage plans and their impact on DSM, curtailment and revenue.
Cash ROIC about 13% (three-year average 13.75% prior year) and cash ROE 17.42% in FY26 versus 16.81% in FY25.
capex_capacity: Added about 1,400 MW of RE Power Sales capacity in FY26 (1,471 MW total including RE Services), versus under 500 MW in the prior year.
Operational capacity rose from about 1,700 MW at start of FY26 to about 3,100 MW at end of FY26.
Of the 2,600 MW contracted but not executed, 100% of capacity expected in FY27 is already contracted; the balance (about 1.2 GW after the 1.5 GW guidance) is for later years.
Solar commissioning deliberately kept light in the July-September 2026 quarter; module procurement to resume from September or October 2026.
Grid uptime was 99.24% in FY26, indicating no material curtailment for the portfolio at that time.
Per-MW EBITDA claimed at 30-35% higher than peers on a DC basis (management's comparison).
demand_pricing: Data and AI share of contracted capacity was 42% (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (260 MW) in April 2024; share unchanged from start of FY26.
Repeat business rate about 74% of new volumes contracted in FY26; 588 customers; 96% of volumes with A-rated or better counterparties.
Average PPA tenor 23.17 years; average lock-in about 18 years; more than 1,100 contracts with no ongoing client dispute per management.
2,600 MW contracted under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, minimal storage); BESS is only about 5-7 MW of the 2,600 MW.
Around 1,600-1,700 MW of the 5,700 MW is structured as contract-for-difference with firm price; management says there is no merchant exposure on that portion.

Management said module price increases from domestic cell requirements are passed to customers through tariffs; customer savings fall from 30-35% to 22-25%, with no margin or volume impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movements in equipment availability or capital costs, but described the situation as volatile.

qa_highlights.question: How much under-construction capacity is CTU, and does the PPA protect against curtailment?
qa_highlights.answer: Each year about one CTU project of about 500 MW is added, with the rest STU; PPAs do not pay for curtailment since corporate customers have no pay-for-performance clauses.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new DSM mechanism on revenues and mitigation?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision; the rules are sub judice and under government discussion, and internal impact estimates are not yet mature. Energy storage is being evaluated as mitigation, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash flow hedge gain of INR414 crore and why is minority interest negative?
qa_highlights.answer: The hedge is a fair-value accounting entry on VPPA/I-REC contract-for-difference derivatives with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs. Minority interest is negative because SPVs are young (under two years) with interest and depreciation weighing on early PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the RE sales EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher BD and overhead costs for 13 MW PPAs across multiple states; margin expected to reach nearly 86% in 3-4 years, still a couple of points below large utilities.

qa_highlights.question: Room for further interest-cost reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees potential from refinancing newer projects, but given macro uncertainty it declined to make bold predictions.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment at the Rajasthan CTU project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30% of power injected; the grid forecasts end of backdown by September 2026, which management advised treating conservatively.

qa_highlights.question: Pipeline and Data and AI mix for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind-solar mix or Data and AI share (42%) to change; it did not target a specific percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Can commissioning rise to 2-2.5 GW a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hopeful the number will grow over time but is not projecting or forecasting a figure.

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%; management sized the risk on the 13% EBITDA share at roughly 2.5% of EBITDA (six months at 40%) to 6.5% (full year at 50%).
DSM rules: industry-wide, under court challenge; impact not quantified; storage-based mitigation decision pending.
Module cost increase from ALMM-related domestic cell requirement from June 2026; procurement for post-June contracts paused until government decision.
Interest rate and FX exposure: about 60% of portfolio is floating rate; management flagged rising-rate risk.
Q1 FY27 commissioning data (due around end-July/early August) to show whether pull-forward demand materialised.
Minority interest losses at SPV level are expected to persist until assets mature (profitability from fourth or fifth year).
summary.management_tone: Confident on contracting, execution and growth, with a defensive stance on regulatory and grid risk. Management declined to give financial guidance or quantify the DSM impact and was evasive on interest-cost reduction, citing macro uncertainty.
